summary: Confirmed DONE. A page load no longer opens /ws/device, requests a second ws-token or runs device.list/simctl. Commit 65af92766 made the client side lazy: connections only register the device client, thread views and the pane start a cheap device.subscribeEvents stream on the main /ws, and the pane lists on mount. /ws/device opens only for screenshots or for older servers. Commit 60633eff3 made the server side cheaper: a 2 s shared simctl listing, a 60 s xcode-select cache and a 5 min xcodebuild -version cache, so availability() plus discover() run simctl once. Both commits are in the Hub-vendored 7bc39eec3. Mobile does not create a device client. The only gap is a narrow behaviour regression: an agent's open-pane request is lost when no thread view has been mounted for more than 60 s.

evidence.note: Connect only calls registerDeviceConnection, which starts nothing. The old unconditional bindDeviceConnection (f1be4abc7 connection.ts:281-283) is gone. reconnect (line 363) only bumps the generation and has no inventory wait.
bindDeviceConnection only subscribes to events. The f1be4abc7 version called refreshInventory() on bind and on every resubscribe.
registerDeviceConnection and ensureDeviceRuntime bind the stream only while something retains it, and unbind after DEVICE_RUNTIME_IDLE_MS = 60 s.
Thread views retain the device runtime so they can consume device.open-pane-requested. DraftChatThreadRouteView.tsx:95 does the same.
subscribeEvents only registers a manager.onEvent listener. It spawns no simctl/xcode process, so retaining it from thread views is cheap.
Inventory (list plus getThreadState) is read only when the pane mounts or the generation changes. The pane is lazily gated in ThreadWorkspacePanel.tsx:1537.

createDirectDeviceRpcTransport sends control RPCs and the event stream on the main socket. The dedicated /ws/device socket is opened lazily (dedicated ??= openDedicated()) only for requestBulk screenshots or after an 'Unknown request tag' fallback, and closes after 60 s idle.

The primary direct client opens /ws/device lazily. Saved environments do the same at service.ts:1159-1182, and hosted shares the main transport at service.ts:959. Mobile's createWsRpcClient calls pass no device client (apps/mobile/src/connection/environmentDriver.ts:333, hostedHub/primaryConnection.ts:218).
The main /ws route serves WsHostedRpcGroup with makeDeviceWsRpcLayer merged in. /ws/device (ws.ts:98-130) stays for older clients only.

DEVICE_LISTING_REUSE_MS = 2 s shares the in-flight simctl listing promise, XCODE_SELECT_CACHE_MS = 60 s and XCODE_VERSION_CACHE_MS = 5 min. Boot refreshes the listing (518, fresh:true) and shutdown drops it (537). IosSimulatorBackend.probeCache.test.ts:50-87 asserts a single xcode-select/simctl.

Tests cover: no list on connect, nothing started before retain, idle unbind, and handover. deviceRpcClient.test.ts:75-159 covers no device socket for control, the older-server fallback and the screenshot-only dedicated socket.

Residual: clearEnvironment (run on idle unbind) drops pendingOpenByThreadKey. DeviceManager.requestOpenPane (apps/server/src/device/DeviceManager.ts:938-946) emits only to live listeners, so open-pane requests are lost while unbound.

fixDefects: Low severity, a narrow behaviour regression and not a perf defect. Before the fix, the event stream was bound for the whole connection, so an agent's device.open-pane-requested for any thread was buffered in pendingOpenByThreadKey and the pane auto-opened when the user later navigated to that thread. Now the stream is bound only while a thread view or the pane retains the environment, and it unbinds 60 s after the last release. The unbind runs store.clearEnvironment (store.ts:159-181), which drops pending open requests. The server emits requestOpenPane to live listeners only (DeviceManager.ts:938-946). So a user who loads the app on, or stays more than 60 s on, a non-thread route (overview, settings) misses the auto-open for an agent's device action. The attachment itself is kept server-side and the pane shows it when opened manually. Out-of-scope notes, also on demand only: (a) on pane mount, list and getThreadState run Android discovery (emulator -list-avds, adb devices -l) twice concurrently with no dedup (AndroidEmulatorBackend.ts:327-329, availability is cached 5 s at 217-222). (b) DeviceManager.publish (1249-1255) runs a full availability plus listing snapshot on every agent activity start and end even with no subscribers, though the 2 s iOS listing reuse bounds it.
implementationSketch: Optional, for the open-pane regression. Simplest option: since subscribeEvents now rides the main socket and spawns nothing (deviceRpc.ts:122-135), bind the event stream for the connection lifetime again. In registerDeviceConnection (runtime.ts:112-147), call bindRegistration immediately, and keep ensureDeviceRuntime only as a no-op or a ref for the pane. This restores buffering at the cost of one idle stream per connection. Alternative that keeps it lazy: in ensureDeviceRuntime's idle timer (runtime.ts:174-179), carry pendingOpenByThreadKey across clearEnvironment (have clearEnvironment take a keepPendingOpen flag). That still loses requests that arrive while unbound. Fully robust variant: on bind, have the server replay the latest unconsumed paneSurfacedUdid per thread through subscribeEvents (DeviceManager already stores paneSurfacedUdid in threadState at line 939). Emit device.open-pane-requested for threads whose surfaced udid has not been acknowledged; this needs a small ack or consume RPC. Tests: extend runtime.test.ts so an open-pane event delivered while no surface retains the environment is still consumable after a thread view retains it. For Android dedup (optional): cache AndroidEmulatorBackend.listDevices with a short shared-promise TTL, as in IosSimulatorBackend.listDevicesUnchecked, invalidated in boot and shutdown. Add a test that one pane-mount refresh (list plus getThreadState) spawns emulator -list-avds once.
decisionReason: The finding's described per-page-load cost is fully removed. The open-pane buffering gap is a small UX regression whose fix (bind the now-cheap stream per connection, or replay on bind) needs no E2EE, auth, Hub protocol or hosted-lifecycle change.
correction: Minor: the auditor called the result 'no defects'. A narrow behaviour regression exists: open-pane requests are dropped when no thread view retained the device runtime in the last 60 s. The auditor's line numbers are slightly off (runtime.ts:112-183, SimulatorPanel.tsx:209-224), and the lazy client wiring is from 65af92766, not only 60633eff3.
